author: Chicago City Wire
title: Final week for 30th Ward residents to submit participatory budget votes
text:
Final week for 30th Ward residents to submit participatory budget votes
30th Ward residents have until the end of this week to submit their first-round votes for participatory budgeting. The process allows community members to help decide how $500,000 in public funds will be allocated for local projects. Eligible residents can participate online or through the ward office.
October 27, 30th Ward residents are reminded that this is the final week to submit their round one votes for the 2026-2027 Participatory Budgeting process. Participatory budgeting is a process that allows community members to directly decide how to allocate public funds in their neighborhood.
According to information from the 30th Ward office, Alderwoman Cruz uses participatory budgeting for three main reasons: community involvement, transparency, and empowerment. "30th Ward residents propose and vote on projects, ensuring that funding addresses local priorities. PB allows greater transparency and accountability in how public funds are spent. By providing neighbors a say in budget decisions, PB empowers communities and strengthens civic engagement," the office said.
Funding for these projects comes from the ward's annual 'menu' money, which is $1.5 million provided each year in the City budget to each ward. Individual alders decide how to spend that money on infrastructure projects, with some using participatory budgeting to allocate these funds. For 2026, 30th Ward residents will vote to allocate up to $500,000 in participatory budgeting funds.
The first round of voting, which takes place in September and October, asks residents what percentage of those funds should be devoted to four categories: parks and public art, residential street resurfacing, curb and gutter repairs, and sidewalk repairs along major streets. Residents are also asked to suggest projects and locations in each category. After this round, the 30th Ward Office will compile suggestions, ensure a geographical balance, and then ask residents to vote for specific projects in a second and final ballot in November and December.
All 30th Ward residents aged 16 or older are eligible to participate in the voting process. For more information or to participate, residents are encouraged to visit the 30th Ward website. The City of Chicago enforces various municipal code violations related to vehicle parking, standing, and operational requirements, with fines ranging from $0 to $250 depending on the offense, according to the City of Chicago.
The participatory budgeting process aims to increase civic engagement and ensure that public funds are used in ways that reflect the priorities of local residents.
